# An edge-case fixture corpus that every compiler and adapter change runs against
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #174, sha256:7253879a468e119189b08924313ad4ac6862aa8cb27c0bfddc180ab47721f984). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Done 2026-10-29 (edge-case fixture corpus: seven fixtures, one iterating test, D123; CI green at f1f9ce6)
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** tooling (a test corpus and one iterating test; ranked by Decider D120)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Product request (2026-10-29): two regressions this week, card 170's dropped inherited failures and an earlier case, passed every test because the Tasks and Orders fixtures have no nested phrases or shared failures; reviewers caught them by reading diffs. The tests should catch this class of regression, not reviewers.
- **Depends on:** none
- **Story:** As Morgan, I want a corpus of small Phrase files, each one a tricky shape with its expected outcome pinned, run by one test on every change, so that this class of regression fails a test and does not depend on me spotting it in a diff.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work; amended by Decider D120):**
  1. Given a folder of small .phrase fixtures chosen with ZOMBIES, When the corpus is read, Then it holds the shapes that card 170 and the earlier regressions touched, one per file with a header comment naming the shape: Many (one failure shared by several endpoints; a multi-level composite phrase; a composite phrase calling a failing phrase), Boundaries (a failure declared by two phrases reached from one endpoint; an endpoint whose first step can raise the same failure name as a later declaring phrase; CRLF line endings) and One (a native-only step); shapes the inline compiler tests already cover (a call cycle, an unknown phrase) are not duplicated
  2. Given each fixture, When a single iterating test builds it with the CLI, Then the expected outcome stored beside it is checked: either the exact diagnostic code and line, or a successful build with the source-map records (kind, name, endpoint, line) and the generated specs passing; the expected outcome files are written by hand and never regenerated from the current output; a fixture that only checks that the build succeeds is not allowed for a shape whose bug would show in the map; adding a case is adding a fixture file and its outcome file, with no change to the test
  3. Given card 170's composite-phrase fix, When it is reverted in a scratch copy (the failure-record lookup that resolves through composite phrases), Then the fixture for the inherited failure fails on its pinned source-map record (the red is shown in the card report), and the corpus test is part of the gate and of CI so every compiler and adapter card runs against it

**Split out (D120):** the remaining Zero, Boundary and Exception shapes (a module with no endpoints, an empty record, the longest allowed name, an undeclared native failure) are card 175.

## Context

- Keep each fixture tiny so the whole corpus runs in well under a minute; build in a temp workspace, never in the repository. Other adapters later reuse the same fixtures and outcome files, so keep the expected outcomes about Phrase behaviour (diagnostics, map records, specs), not about C# text. Cards 165 and 166 touch the emitter and should run against it.
- Follow docs/CODING_GUIDELINES.md: one behaviour per fixture, generated output unchanged unless stated, tests that can fail.
